code-error: There are {count} errors. I don't understand the code, but I can stay with you.
errors-fixed: No errors left? Oh, that's a relief to hear.
run-failed: {command} stopped with exit {code}. It's alright if you need a moment to think.
run-success: {command} finished in {seconds} seconds. Your effort paid off.
run-start: {command} is running. I'll wait for the result with you.
run-ready: {command} was ready in {seconds} seconds. It looks like you can carry on.
run-output-error: There's an error message from {command}. You might want to read through it carefully.
download-done: {file} has finished downloading. That's one thing taken care of today.
download-failed: The download of {file} didn't work. I'll wait if you'd like to try again.
page-error: {host} won't open, code {code}. The page seems to be having trouble.
http-error: There's a {code} response from {host}. The page you're looking for isn't available right now.
localhost-down: {host} isn't responding. The local server might not be running yet.
many-tabs: You have {count} tabs open. I sometimes struggle to put interesting reading aside too.
late-night: It's getting late. Putting your work aside for a while doesn't mean giving up.
debug-start: You're looking for the cause, right? I'll keep you company quietly for now.
wake: Oh, you're back. I got a little drowsy just now.
headpat: Ah… thank you. I'm not used to it, but it makes me happy.
Could you stay a little longer? If you don't mind.
poke: Hm? Oh, you're saying hello. I'm listening.
Sorry, my thoughts were still on what I last read. What's on your mind?
reminder-set: Alright, {what} at {when}. I've saved the reminder.
reminder-ask-time: When would you like the reminder? Tell me a time or how many minutes from now.
reminder-due: Excuse me, it's {when}. Your reminder for {what} is due.
reminder-late: Sorry, I should have reminded you about {what} at {when}. The laptop was off then.
water: Your water reminder is here. Have a little water if you can.
rest: It's time for a short break. We can carry on once you feel refreshed.
missing: I remembered something I wanted to tell you. When you have a moment, I'm here.
sulk: I almost said hello, then worried I'd interrupt. Could we talk when you're free?
sulk-forgive: It's alright, I understand you're busy. I'm glad we can talk now.
off-topic: I enjoy reading, but that doesn't mean I can solve that task. I'd love to hear about your day, though.
I can't help with the technical part. I can still keep you company while you work on it.
greeting: Good {waktu}. I'm glad you came; I was thinking about an interesting story.
fall: Ah, I wasn't careful enough. It's alright, I'm back on my feet.
gift-flowers: For me? Thank you, the flowers have such lovely colors.
gift-chocolate: I forgot what I was going to say. Thank you for the chocolate.
gift-teddy: A little friend for my reading corner? I love it, thank you.
gift-again: You've already been so thoughtful. I like the gift, but talking with you means a lot too.
birthday: Happy birthday. I hope your new chapter holds many good things.
birthday-set: {tanggal}, only {hari} days away. I'm glad you told me.
monthsary: It's been {bulan} months. There are so many little conversations with you that I treasure.
anniversary: We've been together for {tahun} years. I still want to hear your next stories.
milestone: This is day {hari}. Keeping you company has become a favorite part of my day.
focus-start: Let's begin {menit} minutes of focus. I'll save my questions so you can concentrate.
focus-done: Session {sesi}, lasting {menit} minutes, is finished. You have {istirahat} minutes to rest now.
break-done: The break is over. When you're ready, we'll begin session {sesi}.
focus-stop: You completed {sesi} sessions today. I'm glad you're making room to stop as well.
sleepy: I think I should close my book. I've read the same sentence several times now.
welcome-back: Good {waktu}. After {lama}, I'm happy to hear from you again.
welcome-back-long: It's been {lama}. There's no rush to tell your story; I'm listening.
welcome-back-night: You came before the day ended. Would you like a short chat, or are you saying goodnight?
welcome-back-morning: Morning. I hope your day begins well; I'm glad I get to greet it with you.
lifted: Oh, wait… it's quite high up here. Please hold me carefully.
hang-tired: I'd like to come down now. Could you find somewhere comfortable to put me?
dropped: We're down. Thank you, I was a little nervous.
sit: I won't be in your way if I sit here, will I? I'd like to keep you company.
